maintenance_led.reason: Revenue is recurring home medical supplies and equipment (diabetes, sleep, wound care, ostomy) for patients, not repair or maintenance of installed assets.

publicly_funded.reason: Apria and Byram bill Medicare, Medicaid and commercial insurers; the split isn't stated, so government share is unclear.

serial_acquirer.reason: Growth comes mainly from home-care products and services through Apria and Byram; Apria was a single large deal, not a steady roll-up.

mission_critical.reason: Patients depend on ongoing home respiratory, sleep, diabetes and ostomy supplies and equipment; switching disrupts care, insurer networks and prescriptions.

notes: Based on my recollection that Owens & Minor sold its Products & Healthcare Services segment, leaving home-based care; the payer mix is not confirmed.
